title: New York Raises a Park to Hold Back Rising Seas
title_zh: 纽约抬高公园以抵御海平面上升
source_name: UN News — Higher Ground: How New York is raising a park to hold back the sea
summary_zh: 飓风桑迪（2012）过后十四年，纽约东侧海岸韧性工程正把东河公园抬高约三米，并沿曼哈顿滨水带修建防洪墙与闸门；约二十亿美元投资旨在保护逾十一万居民。全球海平面上升速度几乎翻倍，约七亿七千万人住在高潮线五米以内。本文适合积累环境、城市与基础设施类雅思词汇。
paragraphs: Fourteen years after Hurricane Sandy flooded New York City, workers are still answering one promise: never again. On the east side of Manhattan, crews are raising East River Park by as much as three metres and building a hidden floodwall through the rebuilt park. The East Side Coastal Resiliency project, with a smaller scheme to the south, is a roughly two-billion-dollar investment to protect more than 110,000 residents from storm surge and rising seas.

In October 2012, Sandy killed 44 people in the city within 48 hours. Nearly two million New Yorkers lost power, and thousands of patients had to leave hospitals and nursing homes. Public housing near the river stood under at least one storey of water. Officials say the new flood defences are a direct reaction to that disaster — and a way to prepare for worse storms ahead.

Much of the protection is hard to see. Concrete-filled piles go about 30 metres into reclaimed land at the water's edge. When a storm approaches, the park itself needs no moving parts; elsewhere, teams will close 18 floodgates, and farther south nearly 100 flip-up barriers will rise. The design leaves about 76 centimetres for future sea-level rise. About 90 per cent of the system is already in place; temporary barriers can fill gaps until work finishes in 2027.

The threat is not only rare superstorms. The World Meteorological Organization reports that global sea-level rise has nearly doubled since satellite records began in 1993. Warming oceans also fuel stronger tropical storms. For a city with about 840 kilometres of coastline, everyday tides matter too. Without stronger defences, some streets could flood once or even ten times a month — and later, with every daily tide.

New York is not alone. A recent UN report found that nearly ten per cent of the world's people — about 770 million — live less than five metres above high tide. Rising seas mainly damage infrastructure in rich cities such as New York, but they can force communities in low-lying South Asia and Pacific islands to move. UN officials call the project a useful example that other coastal cities should study and copy.

For IELTS learners, this story mixes environment, cities and public investment — three frequent exam themes. Notice how the text moves from a past disaster to concrete engineering, then to global trends and a wider lesson. That problem–solution–evaluation pattern is common in Reading and Writing Task 2.
paragraphs_zh: 飓风桑迪淹没纽约市十四年之后，工人们仍在兑现一句承诺：绝不再重演。在曼哈顿东侧，施工队正把东河公园抬高最多约三米，并在重建后的公园中修建一道隐蔽的防洪墙。东侧海岸韧性工程连同南侧一项较小的配套工程，总投资约二十亿美元，用以保护逾十一万居民免受风暴潮和海平面上升的威胁。
2012年10月，桑迪在48小时内造成该市44人死亡。近两百万纽约人断电，数千名患者不得不撤离医院和疗养院。河边的公共住房至少有一层浸在水下。官员们表示，新的防洪设施是对那场灾难的直接回应——也是为更猛烈的风暴做准备的方式。
大部分防护设施并不显眼。在水边，灌注混凝土的桩基深入填海土地约三十米。风暴来临时，公园本身无需活动部件；其他路段的工作人员将关闭18道防洪闸门，再往南则有近一百道可翻起的屏障升起。设计为未来的海平面上升预留了约76厘米。整套系统约九成已经就位；在2027年工程完工前，可用临时屏障填补缺口。
威胁并不只来自罕见的超级风暴。世界气象组织报告称，自1993年卫星观测开始以来，全球海平面上升速度几乎翻了一倍。变暖的海洋还会助长更强的热带风暴。对一座海岸线约840公里的城市来说，日常潮汐同样重要。如果没有更强的防御，有些街道可能每月被淹一次甚至十次——再往后，甚至会随着每天的潮汐被淹。
纽约并非孤例。联合国最近一份报告发现，全球近百分之十的人口——约七亿七千万人——住在高潮线以上不足五米的地方。海平面上升在纽约这类富裕城市主要破坏基础设施，但在地势低洼的南亚和太平洋岛屿，它可能迫使社区搬迁。联合国官员称，该项目是一个有益范例，其他沿海城市应当研究并加以效仿。
对雅思学习者来说，这篇报道把环境、城市与公共投资这三个常见考试话题结合在一起。注意文章如何从一场过去的灾难讲到具体工程，再到全球趋势与更广的启示。这种「问题—方案—评价」的展开方式，在阅读和写作任务二中经常出现。
